$comment: The AI plugin's native screens, kept in its Apple package (Resources, so Xcode reads it through the plugin manifest symlink) and linked from its Kotlin module (src/android/screens): AI jobs and their status, credits, the hard cap and overage cap, per-member usage, and the staff zones staffOrg and staffUser, the staff AI requests, and the AI spend column the Workspaces list draws (zone staffOrgsListColumn). Bring my site (AGL-4152): the start on ai.import.start, an import job’s waves and its Keep my site or Improve it choice on ai.job. Routes: /api/ai/jobs, /api/ai/site-import/ownership, /api/ai/jobs/{id}/cancel and /resume, /api/ai/billing/credits, /api/ai/billing/overage, /api/ai/allotments, /api/ai/usage, /api/ai/admin/org, /api/ai/admin/user (both with view=prepared), /api/ai/admin/credits, /api/ai/admin/conversations and /api/ai/admin/signals. Grammar: docs/mobile/native-architecture.md §13.

blocks.text:
AglynBot reads your whole site, home page first, as many pages as your plan includes: your main pages first, then collections such as blog posts.
You see what was found, what could not be read and why, and what each wave of up to 10 pages costs before anything is built. Reading your site uses no AI credits.
If your home page cannot be read, nothing is planned and no AI credits are used. You are told why, and you check again once it can be.
Every page comes across with its sections, columns, cards, icons, pictures, tables, tabs and forms, finished the way you choose below. You review each wave and start the next yourself.
Each wave lands in your new site’s preview, where only you and your team can see it, until you make the site public. A site not in preview keeps its pages as drafts. Your current site is not changed.
